p: Little Round Top is UNOCCUPIED by Union infantry — only a signal station on the summit. Warren, Meade's chief engineer, realizes the danger and desperately searches for troops to send there.
Warren's recognition of the Little Round Top crisis and his desperate improvisation to fill it was one of the most consequential individual decisions of the battle.

p.author_line: Ask the Historian site records (chronology commentary)

p: Warren intercepts Vincent's brigade (V Corps) on the march and diverts it to Little Round Top without waiting for formal orders. Vincent personally leads the brigade up the hill.

Vincent's brigade arrives on Little Round Top just ahead of Law's Confederates. Vincent places his regiments on the rocky slope: 16th Michigan right, 44th NY center, 83rd PA center-left, 20th Maine on the extreme left.
15th Alabama (Oates) makes its first assault on 20th Maine's refused left flank. Chamberlain's line bends but holds. Multiple Confederate assaults follow over the next 30-40 minutes.

p.short: Site chronology, Day 2 (Little Round Top south slope)

p: Vincent mortally wounded on Little Round Top. Rice assumes brigade command. Weed's brigade arrives on the summit. Hazlett drags guns up the steep rocky slope. O'Rorke's 140th NY arrives at the summit.
O'Rorke charges downhill without waiting for orders — 140th NY sweeps Confederates off the northern slope of Little Round Top. O'Rorke shot through the neck and killed instantly.

p.short: Site chronology, Day 2 (Little Round Top north slope)

p: Weed killed on the summit. Hazlett shot kneeling beside the dying Weed. Both general and artillery commander die almost simultaneously. Rittenhouse assumes battery command.

p.short: Site chronology, Day 2 (Little Round Top summit)

p: 16th Michigan on Vincent's right begins to waver — brief near-break. The regiment steadies before the line collapses. Critical moment.

p.short: Site chronology, Day 2 (Little Round Top right)

p: CHAMBERLAIN'S BAYONET CHARGE. 20th Maine has expended nearly all ammunition after repulsing multiple assaults. Chamberlain orders a bayonet charge — right-wheel motion sweeping down the hill. 15th Alabama broken and retreating. Nearly 400 Confederate prisoners.

p.short: Site chronology, Day 2 (Little Round Top south slope)

p: McLaws's assault begins. Barksdale's Mississippi brigade charges the Peach Orchard in one of the most dramatic charges of the battle. Barksdale rides ahead of his men on horseback.
Peach Orchard salient collapses. Graham wounded and captured. 141st PA suffers 71% casualties at the apex. III Corps line crumbling from the south toward Cemetery Ridge.

p.short: Site chronology, Day 2 (Peach Orchard / Rose Woods)

p: Kershaw's South Carolina brigade engages in Rose Woods and the Wheatfield. DeTrobriand's Union brigade holds initially. G.T. Anderson's Georgia brigade pressing from the south.
Caldwell's II Corps division rushed south to reinforce the collapsing III Corps. Four brigades — Cross, Kelly (Irish Brigade), Zook, Brooke — advance into the Wheatfield.

p.short: Site chronology, Day 2 (Cemetery Ridge to Wheatfield)

p: Father Corby administers general absolution to the Irish Brigade before the charge. A kneeling army watches from Cemetery Ridge.

p.author_line: Ask the Historian site records (chronology commentary)

p: Father Corby's absolution. The Irish Brigade kneels in the field to receive general absolution before charging into the Wheatfield. One of the most dramatic religious moments of the war.
